records.source: Ταύτην ἤδη, ἀγαπητοί, δευτέραν ὑμῖν γράφω ἐπιστολήν, ἐν αἷς διεγείρω ὑμῶν ἐν ὑπομνήσει τὴν εἰλικρινῆ διάνοιαν, μνησθῆναι τῶν προειρημένων ῥημάτων ὑπὸ τῶν ἁγίων προφητῶν καὶ τῆς τῶν ἀποστόλων ὑμῶν ἐντολῆς τοῦ κυρίου καὶ σωτῆρος, τοῦτο πρῶτον γινώσκοντες ὅτι ἐλεύσονται ἐπ’ ἐσχάτων τῶν ἡμερῶν ἐν ἐμπαιγμονῇ ἐμπαῖκται κατὰ τὰς ἰδίας ἐπιθυμίας αὐτῶν πορευόμενοι καὶ λέγοντες· Ποῦ ἐστιν ἡ ἐπαγγελία τῆς παρουσίας αὐτοῦ;
records.gloss: This now, beloved, second to you I write letter, in which I stir up of you in reminder the sincere mind, \v 2 to remember the having been spoken beforehand words by the holy prophets and the of the apostles of you command of the Lord and Savior, \v 3 this first knowing, that will come in last of the days in scoffing scoffers according to the own desires of them going \v 4 and saying, Where is the promise of the coming of him?
pieces: Dear friends, this is now my second letter to you. In both of them I am trying to rouse your minds to clear thinking by reminding you
to remember what the holy prophets said long ago, and the command of the Lord and Savior that your apostles passed on to you.
Above all, understand this: in the last days scoffers will come, full of scorn, living by their own desires.
They will say, "Where is this promise of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} coming?

L.1: This [is] now, beloved, [the] second letter I am writing to you, in which [letters] I am stirring up your sincere mind by way of reminder,
L.2: to remember the words spoken beforehand by the holy prophets, and the command of the Lord and Savior [given] through your apostles,
L.3: knowing this first, that in [the] last days scoffers will come with scoffing, going according to their own desires
L.4: and saying, "Where is the promise of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} coming?

R.1: Dear friends, this is the second letter I have written to you. In both letters I want to wake up your minds and help you think clearly by reminding you of what you already know.
R.2: Remember the words that God's holy prophets spoke long ago. Remember too the command that the Lord and Savior gave you through your apostles.
R.3: Most of all, you need to know this: in the last days people will come who laugh and sneer. They will live only to please themselves.
R.4: They will say, "Jesus promised to come back. What happened to that promise?

decisions.choice: second letter: this is the second letter the writer has sent these readers, and the reminder runs through both
alternatives: the second part of one letter
decisions.reason: The relative αἷς is plural, so "in which" means both letters. The earlier letter is not named. 1 Peter is the earlier letter known under Peter's name, but the text itself does not say so.

decisions.choice: a sincere mind: thinking that is pure and unmixed, not corrupted by false teaching
decisions.reason: εἰλικρινής describes what is clear and unmixed, tested and found pure. Peter sets the readers' clear thinking against the twisted reasoning of the false teachers (chapter 2). The "reminder" picks up 1:12-15, where he says he will keep reminding them.

decisions.choice: the command of the Lord and Savior, which came to you through your apostles
alternatives: the command of your apostles, who speak for the Lord
decisions.reason: The genitives stack up: the command "of your apostles" and "of the Lord and Savior". The command belongs to the Lord; the apostles are the ones who delivered it. "Your apostles" are those who first brought the message to these readers. Prophets and apostles stand together as the two witnesses to trust, as in 1:16-21.

decisions.choice: the Lord and Savior: Jesus Christ
decisions.reason: One article covers both titles, and the letter uses the same pair for Jesus Christ by name in 1:11, 2:20 and 3:18.

decisions.choice: the last days: the time the church is already living in, before the Lord returns
alternatives: only the final years just before the end
decisions.reason: In the New Testament the last days began with Christ's coming and the gift of the Spirit (Acts 2:17; Hebrews 1:2). Peter speaks of scoffers who "will come", and his readers are expected to meet them; in chapter 2 the false teachers are already among them.

decisions.choice: scoffers with scoffing: the repetition stresses their mocking
decisions.reason: ἐμπαιγμονῇ and ἐμπαῖκται come from the same root, a way of giving emphasis. Their mockery is aimed at the promise that the Lord will return.

decisions.choice: his coming: the promised return of the Lord Jesus
decisions.reason: παρουσία means arrival or presence; Peter has used it for the coming of the Lord Jesus Christ in 1:16. "His" refers back to the Lord and Savior of verse 2. The scoffers' question runs on into the next sentence.

decisions.choice: Dear friends
decisions.reason: ἀγαπητοί means "loved ones", people dear to the writer (and to God). Literal keeps "beloved"; Balanced and Readable say "dear friends", the everyday way to address people one loves. The same choice holds through the chapter (3:8, 3:14, 3:17).

decisions.choice: people who laugh and sneer; "Jesus promised to come back. What happened to that promise?"
alternatives: "Where is the promise of his coming?"
decisions.reason: Readable explains "scoffers" with plain words and turns the question into two short sentences, naming Jesus as the one whose coming was promised (m7).

records.heading: Where is the promise of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} coming?

records.source: ἀφ’ ἧς γὰρ οἱ πατέρες ἐκοιμήθησαν, πάντα οὕτως διαμένει ἀπ’ ἀρχῆς κτίσεως.
records.gloss: From which for the fathers fell asleep, all things thus continue from beginning of creation.
pieces: For ever since our ancestors died, everything goes on just as it has from the beginning of creation."

L.4: For since the fathers fell asleep, all things continue as [they were] from [the] beginning of creation."

R.4: Our ancestors died long ago, and still everything goes on the same way it has since the world was created."

decisions.choice: the fathers: the ancestors of Israel, the patriarchs and those who came after them
alternatives: the first generation of Christians, who had died before the Lord returned
decisions.reason: In the New Testament "the fathers" almost always means the ancestors of Israel (Acts 3:13; Romans 9:5; Hebrews 1:1). The scoffers' argument reaches back to the beginning of creation, which fits that sense. But the complaint is about a promise made by Jesus, so they may mean the first believers who died waiting for him. The words allow both.

decisions.choice: fell asleep: died
decisions.reason: ἐκοιμήθησαν is the common New Testament way of speaking of death, especially the death of God's people (John 11:11-13; 1 Thessalonians 4:13-15).

decisions.choice: the scoffers' argument: nothing has changed since creation, so nothing will change
decisions.reason: διαμένει is present: all things "continue" unchanged. The mockers reason that a world that has never been interrupted never will be. Verses 5-7 answer them: the world has been interrupted before, by the flood.

decisions.choice: our ancestors died
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable give the sense of both expressions (m1, m2) in plain words. "Our" is implied: the speakers count the ancestors as their own.

records.source: λανθάνει γὰρ αὐτοὺς τοῦτο θέλοντας ὅτι οὐρανοὶ ἦσαν ἔκπαλαι καὶ γῆ ἐξ ὕδατος καὶ δι’ ὕδατος συνεστῶσα τῷ τοῦ θεοῦ λόγῳ, δι’ ὧν ὁ τότε κόσμος ὕδατι κατακλυσθεὶς ἀπώλετο·
records.gloss: Escapes for them this willing, that heavens were long ago and earth out of water and through water having been formed by the of the God word, \v 6 through which the then world by water having been flooded perished.
pieces: They choose to overlook this: long ago, by the word of God, the heavens came into being, and the earth was formed out of water and by means of water.
By these, water and word, the world of that time was flooded and destroyed.

L.5: For this escapes [their notice], willingly, that heavens existed long ago and an earth formed out of water and through water by the word of God,
L.6: through which the world of that time, flooded with water, perished.

R.5: But they choose to forget something. Long ago God spoke, and the heavens and the earth came to be. He made the earth rise up out of the water, and water gave it its shape.
R.6: Then God used water and {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} word to flood the world of that time, and it was destroyed.

decisions.choice: they deliberately overlook it: they want to forget
alternatives: this escapes them, as they hold to their view
decisions.reason: θέλοντας can mean "willingly" (they ignore it on purpose) or "maintaining this" (it escapes them while they insist on their view). Both make the same charge: their ignorance is their own choice. λανθάνει "escapes" is echoed in 3:8, where the readers are told not to let something escape them.

decisions.choice: the creation account: the earth rose out of the waters and was set apart by them at God's word
decisions.reason: Genesis 1 begins with the earth under water; God speaks, the waters are divided, and dry land appears (Genesis 1:2, 1:6-10). "By the word of God" is the repeated "God said" of that chapter (compare Psalm 33:6; Hebrews 11:3).

decisions.choice: through which: through water and the word of God together
alternatives: through the heavens and the earth
decisions.reason: ὧν is plural. It most likely gathers up both things just named: the world was destroyed by water, at God's word. Some take it as the waters, from which the land was made and by which it was flooded, or as the heavens and earth. The point is the same: what God made, God can also judge.

decisions.choice: the flood of Noah's day
decisions.reason: The world was "flooded with water" in the time of Noah (Genesis 7:11-23), as Peter has said in 2:5. ἀπώλετο means it perished or was destroyed, not that the earth ceased to exist: the world as it then was came to an end.

decisions.choice: world: the ordered world with the people living in it
decisions.reason: κόσμος here is the world of that time, the inhabited earth and its people, as in 2:5, "the world of the ungodly".

decisions.choice: they choose to overlook; they choose to forget
decisions.reason: Literal keeps "escapes"; Balanced and Readable say what it means (m1). Balanced uses "overlook" again in 3:8 to keep the echo.

decisions.choice: By these, water and word; God used water and his word
decisions.reason: The plural "which" is spelled out, following m3. Readable names God as the one who acted, and rephrases the passive verbs as actions.

records.source: οἱ δὲ νῦν οὐρανοὶ καὶ ἡ γῆ τῷ αὐτῷ λόγῳ τεθησαυρισμένοι εἰσὶν πυρὶ τηρούμενοι εἰς ἡμέραν κρίσεως καὶ ἀπωλείας τῶν ἀσεβῶν ἀνθρώπων.
records.gloss: The but now heavens and the earth by the same word having been stored up are for fire being kept for day of judgment and destruction of the ungodly people.
pieces: But by that same word the present heavens and earth are being held in store for fire. They are kept for the day when {{gender:ungodly people|ungodly men}} will be judged and destroyed.

L.7: But the present heavens and the earth by the same word have been stored up for fire, being kept for [the] day of judgment and destruction of the {{gender:ungodly people|ungodly men}}.

R.7: And by that same word, the heavens and the earth we see now are being kept for fire. God is keeping them for the day when {{gender:people|men}} who do not honor God will be judged and destroyed.

decisions.choice: by the same word: the word of God that made the world and flooded it
decisions.reason: αὐτῷ "same" points back to "the word of God" in verse 5. The world now stands only because God's word holds it, and that word has set its end.

decisions.choice: stored up for fire: kept in reserve to be judged by fire
alternatives: stored up with fire, holding fire within them
decisions.reason: πυρὶ is most naturally "for fire", the end the world is kept for, as the flood was the end of the first world. Fire is the Old Testament picture of God's judgment (Isaiah 66:15-16; Malachi 4:1).

decisions.choice: destruction of the ungodly: their ruin at the judgment
decisions.reason: ἀπώλεια is the same word used of the false teachers' end in 2:1-3; it means ruin and loss, the opposite of being saved. ἀσεβής describes people without reverence for God (2:5-6).

decisions.choice: ungodly people (alternative: ungodly men)
decisions.reason: ἀνθρώπων means human beings, men and women; the gender setting gives the traditional "men".

decisions.choice: people who do not honor God; God is keeping them
decisions.reason: Readable explains "ungodly" (m3) and names God as the one keeping the world (m1).

records.source: Ἓν δὲ τοῦτο μὴ λανθανέτω ὑμᾶς, ἀγαπητοί, ὅτι μία ἡμέρα παρὰ κυρίῳ ὡς χίλια ἔτη καὶ χίλια ἔτη ὡς ἡμέρα μία.
records.gloss: One but this not let escape you, beloved, that one day with Lord like thousand years and thousand years like day one.
pieces: But you, dear friends, must not overlook this one thing: in the Lord's sight a single day is like a thousand years, and a thousand years like a single day.

L.8: But do not let this one [thing] escape you, beloved: that one day with [the] Lord [is] like a thousand years, and a thousand years like one day.

R.8: Dear friends, there is one thing you must keep in mind. To the Lord, a single day is like a thousand years, and a thousand years are like a single day.

decisions.choice: Psalm 90:4: a thousand years in God's sight are like a day that has passed
decisions.reason: The psalm, a prayer of Moses, contrasts God's eternity with the shortness of human life (Psalm 90:4; 89:4 in the Greek Old Testament). Peter turns the saying both ways: time does not limit God, and he does not measure delay as people do. The Lord here is God, as in the psalm.

decisions.choice: do not let this escape you: the readers must not do what the scoffers did
decisions.reason: λανθανέτω repeats the verb of verse 5: the scoffers let a fact escape them; the readers must not.

decisions.choice: God is not bound by time; the saying is not a formula for dating the end
alternatives: a key that turns each day of creation into a thousand years of history
decisions.reason: Peter answers the charge that the Lord is slow (3:9). He is speaking of how God sees time, not giving a scale for counting it.

records.heading: The Lord is patient

records.source: οὐ βραδύνει κύριος τῆς ἐπαγγελίας, ὥς τινες βραδύτητα ἡγοῦνται, ἀλλὰ μακροθυμεῖ εἰς ὑμᾶς, μὴ βουλόμενός τινας ἀπολέσθαι ἀλλὰ πάντας εἰς μετάνοιαν χωρῆσαι.
records.gloss: Not is slow Lord of the promise, as some slowness consider, but is patient toward you, not wanting some to perish but all to repentance to come.
pieces: The Lord is not delaying the promise, as some people think of delay. Rather, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} is being patient with you. He does not want anyone to be destroyed, but wants all people to turn back in repentance.

L.9: [The] Lord is not slow about the promise, as some reckon slowness, but is patient toward you, not willing for any to perish, but for all to make their way to repentance.

R.9: The Lord is not slow to do what {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} promised, though some people think {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} is. He is being patient with you. He does not want anyone to be destroyed. He wants everyone to turn away from their sins and come back to God.

decisions.choice: not slow: the Lord is not late in keeping the promise
decisions.reason: βραδύνω means to be slow or to delay. The scoffers read the long wait as failure (3:4); Peter answers that what looks like delay has another cause.

decisions.choice: patient: holding back judgment to give time
decisions.reason: μακροθυμέω is patience that bears with wrongdoing and waits instead of acting at once, as God waited in the days of Noah (1 Peter 3:20). Verse 15 calls this patience salvation.

decisions.choice: God does not want anyone to perish; he wants all people to come to repentance
alternatives: all of you, the readers, to come to repentance
decisions.reason: πάντας "all" stands against "any". Coming right after "toward you", it could mean all the readers, but the contrast with perishing is general, and Scripture says the same of God's will for everyone (Ezekiel 18:23, 18:32; 1 Timothy 2:4). The sentence states what God wants, not what every person will do.

decisions.choice: perish: be destroyed at the judgment
decisions.reason: ἀπολέσθαι is from the same root as "perished" (3:6) and "destruction" (3:7): to be lost in the judgment God has set.

decisions.choice: be destroyed
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "destroyed" to keep the link with "destroyed" in 3:6-7 (m4). Literal keeps "perish".

decisions.choice: turn away from their sins and come back to God
decisions.reason: Readable explains repentance: a change of mind and life, turning from sin to God.

records.source: ἥξει δὲ ἡμέρα κυρίου ὡς κλέπτης, ἐν ᾗ οἱ οὐρανοὶ ῥοιζηδὸν παρελεύσονται, στοιχεῖα δὲ καυσούμενα λυθήσεται, καὶ γῆ καὶ τὰ ἐν αὐτῇ ἔργα εὑρεθήσεται.
records.gloss: Will come but day of Lord like thief, in which the heavens with a rushing noise will pass away, elements and burning will be dissolved, and earth and the in it works will be found.
pieces: But the day of the Lord will come like a thief. On that day the heavens will vanish with a rushing sound, the elements will be set ablaze and break apart, and the earth and the deeds done on it will be found out.

L.10: But [the] day of [the] Lord will come like a thief, in which the heavens will pass away with a rushing noise, and [the] elements, burning, will be dissolved, and [the] earth and the works in it will be found.

R.10: But the day of the Lord will come suddenly, like a thief. On that day the heavens will disappear with a loud rushing noise. The elements that make up the world will burn and fall apart. The earth and everything people have done on it will be brought out into the open.

decisions.choice: the day of the Lord will come like a thief: suddenly, when no one expects it
decisions.reason: "The day of the Lord" is the Old Testament name for the day God acts in judgment (Joel 2:31; Amos 5:18; Zephaniah 1:14). "Like a thief" is Jesus' own picture of his unexpected return (Matthew 24:43; Luke 12:39), repeated in 1 Thessalonians 5:2 and Revelation 3:3.

decisions.choice: with a rushing noise: a roar, the sound of something rushing past or consumed by fire
decisions.reason: ῥοιζηδόν describes a whizzing, crackling or roaring sound. It is found only here in the New Testament.

decisions.choice: elements: the basic parts the world is made of
alternatives: the heavenly bodies, sun, moon and stars
decisions.reason: στοιχεῖον means the basic parts of something. Here it stands between the heavens and the earth, so it may mean the stuff of the universe or the heavenly bodies, which Isaiah 34:4 says will dissolve. Paul uses the word for the basic principles of this world (Galatians 4:3), but that sense does not fit "burning".

decisions.choice: will be found: the reading of the SBLGNT
decisions.reason: The manuscripts differ at the end of this verse. From general knowledge: "will be found" is the reading of the oldest Greek manuscripts, including Codex Sinaiticus and Codex Vaticanus, and a papyrus (P72) has "will be found dissolved". "Will be burned up" is in Codex Alexandrinus and most later manuscripts, and became the familiar reading. Some early versions read "will not be found", and Codex Ephraemi reads "will disappear". "Will be found" is the hardest reading, and copyists seem to have changed it to something easier. The SBLGNT text is followed here. Reviewers must check this against the SBLGNT apparatus before the sentence is marked meaning reviewed.

decisions.choice: will be found: laid open before God for judgment, with nothing hidden
alternatives: found to remain, surviving the fire
decisions.reason: With the heavens gone and the elements dissolved, the earth and what was done on it stand exposed to God. εὑρίσκω is used this way in 3:14, where the readers are to be "found" spotless by him; compare 1 Corinthians 3:13, where fire shows what each person's work is.

decisions.choice: works: the deeds people have done on the earth
alternatives: the things made on the earth
decisions.reason: ἔργον can mean deeds or things made. Read with "will be found" (m5), it most likely means human deeds brought to judgment, but it may mean everything on the earth.

decisions.choice: suddenly, like a thief
decisions.reason: Readable adds "suddenly" so the picture is clear (m1).

decisions.choice: will be found out; will be brought out into the open
decisions.reason: Balanced keeps "found" to stay close to the Greek and to echo 3:14, adding "out" to show the sense of exposure (m5). Readable says it plainly.

records.source: Τούτων οὕτως πάντων λυομένων ποταποὺς δεῖ ὑπάρχειν ὑμᾶς ἐν ἁγίαις ἀναστροφαῖς καὶ εὐσεβείαις, προσδοκῶντας καὶ σπεύδοντας τὴν παρουσίαν τῆς τοῦ θεοῦ ἡμέρας, δι’ ἣν οὐρανοὶ πυρούμενοι λυθήσονται καὶ στοιχεῖα καυσούμενα τήκεται·
records.gloss: These thus all being dissolved, what sort ought to be you in holy conducts and godlinesses, \v 12 awaiting and hastening the coming of the of the God day, because of which heavens being set on fire will be dissolved and elements burning melt.
pieces: Since everything is to be dissolved in this way, think what sort of people you ought to be! Live holy and godly lives,
as you wait for the coming of the day of God and hurry it on. That day will set the heavens on fire and dissolve them, and the elements will melt in the heat.

L.11: Since all these things are being dissolved in this way, what sort [of people] you ought to be in holy conduct and godliness,
L.12: waiting for and hastening the coming of the day of God, because of which [the] heavens, set on fire, will be dissolved, and [the] elements, burning, melt!

R.11: All these things will be destroyed like this. So think about what kind of people you should be! Live holy lives that honor God,
R.12: as you wait for the day of God. Live in a way that makes that day come sooner. On that day the heavens will catch fire and be destroyed, and everything the world is made of will melt in the heat.

decisions.choice: what sort of people you ought to be: an exclamation that calls for a holy life
alternatives: a question: what sort of people ought you to be?
decisions.reason: ποταποὺς can open a question or an exclamation. The SBLGNT does not punctuate it as a question, and the answer follows at once: holy conduct and godliness. Either way it presses the readers to live in the light of the end.

decisions.choice: holy conduct and godliness: holy ways of living and acts of devotion to God
decisions.reason: Both nouns are plural, pointing to many acts and habits of holy living and reverence for God. εὐσέβεια is the godliness of 1:3, 1:6-7, the opposite of the "ungodly" of 3:7.

decisions.choice: hastening: helping to bring the day sooner, by repentance and holy living
decisions.reason: σπεύδω usually means to hurry. With an object it can mean to hurry something on, or to be eager for it. Verse 9 says the Lord waits so that people may repent, and Acts 3:19-21 links repentance with the coming of the times of refreshing; so the readers' lives can speed the day. The other reading takes the word as eager longing, close to "waiting for". This draft follows the first reading.

decisions.choice: the coming of the day of God: the same day as the day of the Lord (3:10)
decisions.reason: "The day of God" is a rare phrase in the New Testament; here it means the day of the Lord just described. παρουσία is the same word as "coming" in 3:4: the scoffers mocked it; the readers wait for it.

decisions.choice: because of which: the day of God brings the dissolving of the heavens and elements
decisions.reason: δι ἣν means "on account of which": the day is the cause. The verb "melt" is present in form, but it describes what will happen then, as the parallel "will be dissolved" shows. The language recalls Isaiah 34:4.

decisions.choice: two sentences: an exclamation, then a command
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable break the long Greek sentence, turning the description of holy living into a command so it reads clearly (m1).

decisions.choice: Live in a way that makes that day come sooner.
decisions.reason: Readable follows m3 and explains how the day is hastened. It is an expansion on a debated word, so reviewers should weigh it with m3.

records.heading: Waiting for the day of God

records.source: καινοὺς δὲ οὐρανοὺς καὶ γῆν καινὴν κατὰ τὸ ἐπάγγελμα αὐτοῦ προσδοκῶμεν, ἐν οἷς δικαιοσύνη κατοικεῖ.
records.gloss: New but heavens and earth new according to the promise of him we await, in which righteousness dwells.
pieces: But we are looking forward to what {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} promised: new heavens and a new earth, where righteousness is at home.

L.13: But new heavens and a new earth, according to {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} promise, we are waiting for, in which righteousness dwells.

R.13: But we are waiting for new heavens and a new earth, just as God promised. Righteousness will be at home there.

decisions.choice: new heavens and a new earth: God's promise in Isaiah
decisions.reason: God says in Isaiah 65:17 and 66:22 that he will create new heavens and a new earth. Revelation 21:1 sees it fulfilled. "His promise" is that promise of God, which the scoffers' talk of "the promise" (3:4) ignores.

decisions.choice: new: made new, a world of a different order
alternatives: merely another world like this one
decisions.reason: καινός speaks of what is new in kind and fresh, not just recent. The fire of judgment ends the present world, but God's purpose is a renewed creation.

decisions.choice: righteousness dwells there: what is right before God will be settled there for good
decisions.reason: κατοικέω means to settle and live in a place as one's home. In the present world the ungodly are at home (3:7); in the new one, righteousness will be.

decisions.choice: just as God promised
decisions.reason: Readable names God as the one who made the promise (m1).

records.source: Διό, ἀγαπητοί, ταῦτα προσδοκῶντες σπουδάσατε ἄσπιλοι καὶ ἀμώμητοι αὐτῷ εὑρεθῆναι ἐν εἰρήνῃ, καὶ τὴν τοῦ κυρίου ἡμῶν μακροθυμίαν σωτηρίαν ἡγεῖσθε, καθὼς καὶ ὁ ἀγαπητὸς ἡμῶν ἀδελφὸς Παῦλος κατὰ τὴν δοθεῖσαν αὐτῷ σοφίαν ἔγραψεν ὑμῖν, ὡς καὶ ἐν πάσαις ταῖς ἐπιστολαῖς λαλῶν ἐν αὐταῖς περὶ τούτων, ἐν αἷς ἐστιν δυσνόητά τινα, ἃ οἱ ἀμαθεῖς καὶ ἀστήρικτοι στρεβλοῦσιν ὡς καὶ τὰς λοιπὰς γραφὰς πρὸς τὴν ἰδίαν αὐτῶν ἀπώλειαν.
records.gloss: Therefore, beloved, these things awaiting, be diligent spotless and blameless by him to be found in peace, \v 15 and the of the Lord of us patience salvation consider, just as also the beloved of us brother Paul according to the having been given to him wisdom wrote to you, \v 16 as also in all the letters speaking in them about these things, in which are hard to understand some things, which the untaught and unstable twist as also the other writings to the own of them destruction.
pieces: So, dear friends, while you wait for these things, work hard to be found by {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} spotless and without fault, and at peace.
Regard our Lord's patience as salvation. Paul, our dear brother, wrote to you about this too, with the wisdom God gave him.

He does so in all his letters when he speaks of these things. Some things in them are hard to grasp, and people who are untaught and unsteady bend them out of shape, as they bend the other Scriptures, and so bring about their own destruction.

L.14: Therefore, beloved, waiting for these things, be diligent to be found by {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} spotless and blameless, in peace,
L.15: and consider the patience of our Lord [to be] salvation, just as our beloved brother Paul also wrote to you according to the wisdom given to him,
L.16: as [he does] also in all [his] letters, speaking in them about these things, in which are some things hard to understand, which the untaught and unstable twist, as [they do] also the other scriptures, to their own destruction.

R.14: So, dear friends, while you are waiting for these things, try hard to live pure lives with nothing wrong in them. Then when the Lord comes, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will find you living in peace.
R.15: Remember that our Lord is patient because {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} wants people to be saved. Our dear brother Paul also wrote to you about this, with the wisdom that God gave him.
R.16: He writes about these things in all his letters. Some things in his letters are hard to understand. People who have not been taught well and do not stand firm twist what he wrote to make it mean something else. They do the same with the rest of the Scriptures. In the end it will destroy them.

decisions.choice: spotless and blameless: pure, with nothing to stain or spoil them
decisions.reason: The words describe an unblemished sacrifice (1 Peter 1:19). They are the reverse of the false teachers, whom Peter calls stains and blemishes (2:13).

decisions.choice: found by him: found so by the Lord at his coming
decisions.reason: αὐτῷ names the one who finds them, the Lord whose day has just been described. "Found" picks up 3:10: on that day everything will be found as it is.

decisions.choice: in peace: at peace with God and living in peace, with nothing to fear
decisions.reason: Peace is the greeting of 1:2 and the state of those who are ready for the Lord's coming.

decisions.choice: the Lord's patience means salvation: the time he gives is for people to be saved
decisions.reason: This answers the scoffers once more (3:4, 3:9). What they call slowness is the time the Lord gives for people to repent and be saved.

decisions.choice: Paul wrote to these readers about the same thing; the letter is not named
alternatives: a particular letter such as Romans
decisions.reason: Peter does not say which letter he means. Paul speaks of God's patience leading to repentance in Romans 2:4, and of being blameless at the Lord's coming in 1 Thessalonians 5:23 and 1 Corinthians 1:8. "Our beloved brother" shows Peter honoring Paul as a fellow apostle (compare Galatians 2:9).

decisions.choice: in which: in the letters, following the SBLGNT
alternatives: in which things: in the subjects Paul writes about
decisions.reason: αἷς is feminine and refers to the letters. From general knowledge, many later manuscripts read οἷς, a form that would refer to the matters Paul discusses. The sense changes little. Reviewers must check this against the SBLGNT apparatus.

decisions.choice: the untaught and unstable twist them: people without teaching and without a firm footing distort them
decisions.reason: στρεβλόω means to wrench or twist, as on a rack. ἀστήρικτος, "unstable", echoes 1:12 and 3:17: the readers are to stand firm, unlike these people.

decisions.choice: the other scriptures: Paul's letters are counted with the Scriptures
alternatives: the other writings, in a general sense
Paul's letters are compared with the Scriptures, not counted among them
decisions.reason: Everywhere else in the New Testament γραφή means the sacred Scriptures. "The other" (λοιπὰς) puts Paul's letters in the same group: people twist them just as they twist the rest of Scripture. The sentence shows that Paul's letters were being read and valued alongside the Scriptures of Israel when this letter was written; it does not say which other writings were included.

decisions.choice: to their own destruction: the twisting leads to their ruin at the judgment
decisions.reason: ἀπώλεια is the destruction of the ungodly in 3:7 and of the false teachers in 2:1-3.

decisions.choice: three English sentences after the command
decisions.reason: The long Greek sentence is broken so the remarks about Paul and his letters can be followed.

decisions.choice: the wisdom God gave him
decisions.reason: The passive implies that God gave the wisdom. Readable says the same.

decisions.choice: when the Lord comes, he will find you; because he wants people to be saved
alternatives: to be found by him; consider the patience of our Lord salvation
decisions.reason: Readable names the Lord as the one who finds them (m2) and explains how patience means salvation (m4).

records.heading: Be found at peace

records.source: ὑμεῖς οὖν, ἀγαπητοί, προγινώσκοντες φυλάσσεσθε ἵνα μὴ τῇ τῶν ἀθέσμων πλάνῃ συναπαχθέντες ἐκπέσητε τοῦ ἰδίου στηριγμοῦ, αὐξάνετε δὲ ἐν χάριτι καὶ γνώσει τοῦ κυρίου ἡμῶν καὶ σωτῆρος Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ.
records.gloss: You therefore, beloved, knowing beforehand, guard yourselves so that not by the of the lawless error having been carried away you fall from the own firmness, \v 18 grow but in grace and knowledge of the Lord of us and Savior Jesus Christ.
pieces: So, dear friends, since you have been told this in advance, be on your guard. Do not let the error of lawless people sweep you along and knock you off your own firm footing.
Instead, keep growing in the grace that comes from our Lord and Savior Jesus {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}}, and in knowing {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.

L.17: You therefore, beloved, knowing [this] beforehand, guard yourselves, so that you do not, carried away by the error of the lawless, fall from your own firm footing,
L.18: but grow in grace and knowledge of our Lord and Savior Jesus {{christos:Christ|Messiah}}.

R.17: Dear friends, now you know these things ahead of time. So be careful. Do not let the false ideas of people who reject God's law carry you away. Do not let them pull you down from the firm place where you stand.
R.18: Instead, keep growing in the grace that our Lord and Savior Jesus {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} gives, and keep getting to know {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} better.

decisions.choice: knowing beforehand: warned in advance by this letter
decisions.reason: προγινώσκω here means to know ahead of time. Peter has told them what the scoffers and false teachers will say (3:3; 2:1), so they will not be taken by surprise.

decisions.choice: carried away by the error of the lawless: swept along by the false teachers' wrong way
decisions.reason: ἄθεσμος describes people who keep no law or principle; Peter used it of the people of Sodom (2:7). πλάνη is wandering from the truth, and συναπάγομαι is to be carried off together with others.

decisions.choice: your own firm footing: the stable place where you stand in the truth
decisions.reason: στηριγμός is firmness or a fixed position. It answers "unstable" in 3:16 and recalls 1:12, where the readers are "established in the truth".

decisions.choice: grace and knowledge of our Lord: grace that comes from him and knowledge of him
alternatives: both grace and knowledge belong to the Lord in the same way
decisions.reason: The genitive "of our Lord" goes with both nouns, but differently: the Lord gives grace, and he is the one known. Knowing him is the theme the letter began with (1:2-3, 1:8).

decisions.choice: grace that comes from ...; and in knowing him
alternatives: grace and knowledge of our Lord
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable spell out the two senses of the genitive (m4).

decisions.choice: the false ideas of people who reject God's law
decisions.reason: Readable explains "lawless" (m2) and "error" in plain words.

records.source: αὐτῷ ἡ δόξα καὶ νῦν καὶ εἰς ἡμέραν αἰῶνος. ἀμήν.
records.gloss: To him the glory both now and to day of eternity. Amen.
pieces: May glory be {{deity_pronoun:his|His}}, both now and to the day of eternity. Amen.

L.18: To {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} [be] the glory, both now and to [the] day of eternity. Amen.

R.18: May all glory be {{deity_pronoun:his|His}}, now and on that day that will never end. Amen.

decisions.choice: one record: the doxology and its closing Amen
decisions.reason: The SBLGNT puts a full stop before ἀμήν, but the Amen is the response that seals the doxology, not a sentence of its own. It is kept with the words it answers, as in Philippians 4:20.

decisions.choice: to him: to Jesus Christ
decisions.reason: αὐτῷ refers to "our Lord and Savior Jesus Christ" just named. Most New Testament doxologies give glory to God; this one gives it to Christ, as 2 Timothy 4:18 and Revelation 1:5-6 also do.

decisions.choice: a prayer of praise: may the glory be his
alternatives: a statement: the glory is his
decisions.reason: The Greek has no verb. Doxologies like this are usually read as wishes or praise ("be"), though they also state what is true.

decisions.choice: the day of eternity: the day that begins the age to come and never ends
decisions.reason: The phrase is found only here in the New Testament. It recalls "the day of God" (3:12): the day that brings in eternity, which has no evening.

decisions.choice: Amen, following the SBLGNT
decisions.reason: From general knowledge, a few manuscripts, Codex Vaticanus among them, end without the Amen; most include it. Reviewers must check this against the SBLGNT apparatus.

decisions.choice: on that day that will never end
decisions.reason: Readable explains the phrase (m4).
